terra.problem: The claim that a census would not have told Jehoshaphat much because he knew an army was coming is an unsupported conclusion.
The text does not say nobody in Judah was in a party mood, or that Jehoshaphat proclaimed the fast because he was alarmed.
The image of every road filling up at once adds timing and travel details the text does not give.
The passage describes God giving the land forever, but does not mention an old promise. A claim about a promise from elsewhere needs a reference.
Moses's identity as Israel's leader and the statement that Abraham came earlier are facts from outside this passage without references.
David's identity as Israel's king is a fact from outside this passage without a reference.
The passage says what the people said God would do; it does not identify those words as a promise from God.
Saying Jehoshaphat has nothing hidden makes a claim about him that the text does not establish.
Jehoshaphat tells the people to believe God's prophets, but the text does not say he is specifically pointing back to Jahaziel's words.
The text places singers before the army but does not say there was not one weapon in the lead.
The explanation is a plain recap without Papa Dorin's voice or personality.
The text says when the shouts and praises began, but does not establish that Judah was still singing as the battle was handled.
The text does not say Judah was still on the march or that none of them watched the fighting.
The text does not specify that all the fighting happened while Judah was still on its way.
The text says they found more than they could carry away, not that this was still the case after three days of gathering.
The text says the kingdoms heard what happened, but does not say how fast the word traveled.
The passage does not say whether the nations stormed back.
The line about quiet being hard to bake has no clear comparison or joke logic.
The reference to a single day adds timing that the passage does not give; the events described span several days.
The text says the kingdom was at peace, but does not say Judah was paying nobody.
